patients.summary: Retired long-haul trucker with COPD group C, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and CAD after a 2019 LAD stent, who joins in late 2022 right after quitting a 50 pack-year habit. In October 2024 a papillary muscle rupture after an acute MI needs emergent mitral repair; in June 2025 he has cardiogenic shock after a right hip replacement; in February 2026 he takes old and new metoprolol together after a COPD admission and lands in the ED bradycardic.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66M here to establish. Drove a long-haul rig for about 35 years, retired at 64. Former practice hard to reach; wants one doctor who picks up.

Lungs: COPD, told 'group C' by his old PCP, had breathing tests there years ago. On tiotropium every morning and albuterol, which he uses maybe 2-3x a week, more in cold weather. Has had flares needing prednisone in the past, none this year. Walks the loop around his block most days, winded on hills.

Heart: MI in 2019, taken to the cath lab at an outside hospital and got a stent in the LAD. Sees an outside cardiologist yearly. No angina since. On aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 25.

BP: told high years ago, managed on the metoprolol.

Also had a bronchoscopy with a lung wash 'when I was in the hospital once' - can't remember the year or why. Will look for it in old records.

Tobacco: about 50 pack-years. Quit last month, cold turkey, after his brother pushed him. No patches or gum. No cravings he can't manage. Alcohol: a drink or so a month. No drugs.
Allergies: none to medicines.
Family: father died at 61 of a heart attack. Mother alive, high blood pressure and osteoporosis, in her late 80s. Older brother had bypass surgery for blockages.
Social: divorced, lives by himself, independent with everything, still drives.

ROS: chronic exertional dyspnea at baseline, occasional morning cough with clear sputum. No chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, ankle swelling, fevers or weight loss.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Comfortable, talking in full sentences. No JVD. Heart regular, normal S1 S2, no murmur. Lungs with mildly prolonged expiration, scattered faint end-expiratory wheeze, no crackles. Abdomen benign. Legs without edema, pulses 2+.
PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P
1. COPD, group C per prior records - stable on tiotropium plus PRN albuterol. Inhaler technique reviewed, good. Will get spirometry values from old office.
2. CAD s/p MI 2019 with LAD DES - asymptomatic. Continue aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol.
3. HTN - at goal today.
4. Hyperlipidemia - lipids today.
5. Former smoker, quit 10/2022, 50 pk-yr - congratulated. Eligible for annual lung screening; low-dose CT ordered for January.
6. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids; one-time hep C and HIV screens. High-dose flu vaccine given today. Will check old records for colonoscopy and vaccine history.
RTC 4 months.

- Separate older inpatient note references a diagnostic bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage during that stay; indication and results not in the packet.
- Screening colonoscopy 2018, normal, repeat in 10 years.
- Last flu shot 2021. Pneumococcal and shingles vaccines: no record.

No allergies listed.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: annual lung cancer screening, 66-year-old former smoker, 50 pack-years, quit 2022. Baseline exam.
Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Mild centrilobular emphysema in the upper lobes. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal; coronary stent in the LAD with coronary artery calcification. Mediastinal and hilar nodes not enlarged. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with LDCT in 12 months.

conditions.label: Acute mitral regurgitation due to papillary muscle rupture

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia. Q waves and other findings of the prior myocardial infarction. No new ST-segment or T-wave changes compared with the prior tracing.
reports.conclusion: No new changes since prior MI.

reports.text: Portable AP upright view. Bilateral perihilar and basilar airspace opacity with interstitial thickening and vascular congestion. No pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette within limits for technique. Coronary stent.

CT angiography of the chest, aortic dissection protocol. Thoracic aorta normal in caliber with no intimal flap, intramural hematoma or penetrating ulcer. No pulmonary embolism to the segmental level. Bilateral ground-glass and interlobular septal thickening with small dependent effusions, consistent with pulmonary edema. Background upper-lobe emphysema. Coronary stent.

Urgent limited study at the bedside. Flail mitral valve leaflets with severe mitral regurgitation. Left atrium dilated. Left ventricular systolic function not formally quantified on this limited study. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Flail mitral leaflets with severe mitral regurgitation; dilated left atrium. Cardiac surgery consulted.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 10/14/2024. Received by fax 10/17/2024.

CC: chest pain, short of breath.
HPI: 68-year-old man woke and within minutes developed crushing, ripping chest pain that went straight through to his back, with sudden breathlessness. Brought by ambulance. History of CAD with LAD stent (2019), COPD, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 25, tiotropium, albuterol PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: ex-smoker (quit 2022), rare alcohol.

Triage: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air.
Exam: sweating, in obvious distress. Crackles to the mid-lung fields on both sides. New loud holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating into the axilla. Extremities without asymmetry in pulses.

ECG: sinus tach, no new changes from his prior infarct.
CXR: pulmonary edema.
CTA chest (dissection protocol, given the pain description): no dissection.
Bedside TTE: flail mitral leaflets, severe MR, dilated LA.

Impression: acute severe mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture; pulmonary edema with hypoxemia and hypotension.
Course: high-flow oxygen; cardiology and cardiac surgery at bedside. Taken for emergent surgery.
Disposition: admitted, cardiac surgery service.

events.reason: Acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiac surgery service. Admitted 10/14/2024, discharged 10/23/2024. Received 11/20/2024 in response to records request.

Principal diagnosis: acute mitral regurgitation due to papillary muscle rupture following acute myocardial infarction.
Secondary: CAD s/p prior MI and LAD DES (2019), COPD, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

Procedure: 10/14/2024 emergent mitral valve repair with annuloplasty ring via median sternotomy.

Course: presented through our ED with acute pulmonary edema and hypotension; echo showed flail mitral leaflets with severe MR. Acute MI felt to be the cause of the papillary muscle rupture; ECG unchanged from his old infarct. Went to the OR the same day. Extubated postoperative day 1. Chest tubes out day 3. Uneventful recovery on the step-down unit, ambulating independently by discharge.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily, albuterol inhaler as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiac surgery wound check 2 weeks; cardiology 6-8 weeks with echo; PCP 1 week.
Sternal precautions 6-8 weeks, no driving 4 weeks.

documents.title: Patient call: recent hospital stay
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know he was in the hospital 10/14-10/23. Says he had 'a heart valve blow out' and had open-heart surgery to fix it the same day. Home since Wednesday, neighbor driving him. Sternal incision dry, no fever. Breathing better than before surgery, mild ache at the incision that is easing. No paperwork other than a med list - same 5 meds as before. Post-discharge visit booked Tuesday 10/29 with PCP. Records request sent to the hospital for ED note, discharge summary and op note.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after mitral valve repair

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here 6 days after discharge. Only the ED fax came in so far (10/17); discharge summary and op note requested, not yet received. His account plus the ED record: woke 10/14 with sudden severe pain through to the back and couldn't breathe; ED found a flail mitral valve with severe leak from a ruptured papillary muscle; dissection ruled out by CT; emergent mitral repair with a ring that day. He was told it went with 'another heart attack.'

Now: tired, sleeping in a recliner the first few nights, back in bed now. Incision a little sore. Walking the hallway and short loops outside. No fever, no drainage, no palpitations. Breathing better than his usual. Taking all 5 meds; no new prescriptions given at discharge.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, down about 4 kg from September. Sternotomy healing, edges approximated, no erythema, sternum stable. Heart regular, no murmur heard. Lungs with decreased bases, no crackles. No edema.

A/P:
1. S/p emergent mitral valve repair with annuloplasty ring for papillary muscle rupture after acute MI. Recovering. Sternal precautions, no driving for now per surgery. BMP and CBC today. Surgery wound check next week; cardiology with echo in December.
2. CAD - meds unchanged: aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 25.
3. COPD - stable.
Will re-request hospital records. Call with fever, wound drainage, worsening breathlessness or leg swelling.

documents.title: Blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count and kidney tests from Tuesday are normal - no sign of anemia after the surgery. Keep walking a little more each day.

conditions.label: Acute mitral regurgitation due to papillary muscle rupture

reports.text:
Indication: 8 weeks after mitral valve repair with annuloplasty ring.
Left ventricle normal in size; LVEF 50% by biplane method. Mitral annuloplasty ring well seated with no rocking. No significant residual mitral regurgitation; no mitral stenosis. Aortic valve trileaflet without stenosis or regurgitation. Right ventricle normal size and function. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Well-seated mitral annuloplasty ring without significant residual mitral regurgitation. LVEF 50%.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit 12/12/2024.

Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Lewandowski in follow-up eight weeks after his emergent mitral valve repair with ring annuloplasty for papillary muscle rupture in the setting of an acute MI. He is walking 20 minutes daily, no angina, no orthopnea or edema. Sternum has healed.

Blood pressure and heart rate well controlled. Lungs clear. Regular rhythm, no murmur. No edema.

Echo today: ring well seated, no significant residual MR, LVEF 50%.

Plan: continue aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 25 mg. May resume driving and normal activity. See me in 6 months.
Allergies: none known.

With regards,
Cardiology

documents.title: Hip pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Right hip has bothered him for months, he thinks since last summer, and it got harder to ignore once he started walking every day for his heart. Deep ache in the groin and outer hip, worse after a mile, stiff getting out of the car, better with rest. No fall or injury. No back pain, numbness or weakness. No fever.
Heart side: doing well, cardiology happy in December. Breathing stable.

Exam: antalgic gait on the right. Right hip internal rotation limited and reproduces groin pain; FABER uncomfortable on the right. Left hip full and painless. Lumbar spine nontender, straight leg raise negative. Strength and sensation normal in the legs. Distal pulses intact.

A/P: right hip pain with the pattern of osteoarthritis. Wants a surgical opinion now rather than months of trial-and-error. Referred to orthopedics; they will image in their office. Cardiac history means any surgery needs clearance - will coordinate when the time comes.

documents.title: Orthopedic Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic practice. Seen 3/13/2025 at the request of his primary care physician.

History: 68-year-old retired truck driver with progressive right groin and lateral hip pain for most of a year, now limiting his walking program. Cardiac history notable for mitral valve repair in October 2024 and a 2019 LAD stent. COPD. NKDA.

Exam: antalgic gait. Right hip flexion limited, with painful, restricted internal rotation. Neurovascularly intact.

Radiographs (AP pelvis, right hip AP/lateral, taken today): right hip joint space narrowing with osteophyte formation, consistent with osteoarthritis. Left hip preserved.

Impression: primary osteoarthritis, right hip.
Plan: discussed options. Given his functional goals, he would like to proceed with right total hip arthroplasty. Will schedule for June pending medical and cardiology clearance. Pre-op education class.

Thank you for the referral.
Orthopedic Surgery

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op eval, right THA scheduled 6/18 with outside orthopedics.

Functional capacity: walks about a mile on level ground, slowed by the hip not by breath or chest. Climbs a flight of stairs without stopping. No angina, orthopnea, PND, syncope or palpitations.
Pulmonary: COPD, no flare in more than a year, rescue inhaler a couple times a week.
Anesthesia: tolerated cardiac surgery in October without problems.
Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 25, tiotropium, albuterol PRN. NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Lungs with prolonged expiration, no wheeze today. Heart regular, no murmur. Sternotomy well healed. No edema.
ECG: sinus, old infarct, unchanged from October.
CBC and BMP drawn.

Assessment: elevated-risk surgery candidate because of his CAD and recent mitral repair, but functionally good and without active cardiac symptoms; COPD stable. Defer to cardiology for final clearance; appointment set next week. Continue beta-blocker through surgery. Aspirin plan per surgeon and cardiology. Bring inhalers to the hospital; use albuterol the morning of surgery if needed.

documents.title: Cardiology Pre-operative Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit 5/29/2025.

Re: right total hip arthroplasty planned 6/18/2025.

Mr. Lewandowski is seven months out from mitral repair with ring annuloplasty after papillary muscle rupture, with an LVEF of 50% and no significant residual MR on his December echo. He has no angina or heart failure symptoms and good exercise tolerance limited by the hip. ECG from his PCP's office is unchanged.

Assessment: acceptable cardiac risk for the planned orthopedic surgery. No further preoperative testing needed. Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg and atorvastatin perioperatively; continue aspirin 81 mg through surgery.

Cardiology

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (Orthopedics / Cardiac ICU)
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 6/18/2025, discharged 6/27/2025. Copy received 8/6/2025 after second records request.

Admitting: elective right total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis (orthopedic surgery). Procedure 6/18, uncomplicated per brief op report (full operative note not included).

Hospital course: on postoperative day 2 (6/20) early morning he became acutely short of breath and hypotensive without chest pain. BP 85/50, RR 28, working to breathe. Neck veins distended, crackles to the mid-lung fields bilaterally, S3, cool extremities, 1+ pitting edema of both lower legs. Transferred to the cardiac ICU.
Labs: troponin I 8 ng/mL (ref <0.04), BNP 900 pg/mL (ref <100). ABG pH 7.32 / PaCO2 45 / PaO2 60 / HCO3 22. CBC and BMP normal.
ECG: no new changes vs preoperative.
Pulmonary artery catheter: cardiac index 1.8 L/min/m2, PCWP 28 mmHg.

Diagnoses: cardiogenic shock; acute hypoxemic respiratory failure without hypercapnia.
Treatment: dobutamine infusion and IV furosemide with supplemental oxygen; metoprolol held. Hemodynamics improved over 72 hours; dobutamine weaned off 6/23, PA catheter removed, IV diuretic stopped. Transferred to the orthopedic floor 6/24. Metoprolol succinate 25 mg resumed 6/26. Worked with PT, weight bearing as tolerated.

Discharge 6/27 to home with home PT.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, tiotropium daily, albuterol as needed. No new medications.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: orthopedics 2 weeks; cardiology 6-8 weeks; PCP within 1 week.

Outside cardiology group. Visit 8/21/2025.

Dear colleague,
Mr. Lewandowski returns two months after the episode of cardiogenic shock on postoperative day 2 of his right hip replacement, managed in the cardiac ICU with inotrope and diuretic. He has recovered well: walking without a cane, no orthopnea, no edema, no chest pain.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, 69M. Big year: hip replacement in June complicated by postoperative cardiogenic shock, now recovered; cardiology saw him in August with no changes.
HRA: independent ADLs/IADLs, back to driving, walking 30-40 min most days with the new hip - says it's the best he's walked in years. No falls since surgery. PHQ-2 1 (tired in July, better now). Recall 3/3.
Tobacco: quit nearly 3 years. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month.
Meds reviewed with bottles: aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 25, tiotropium, albuterol PRN. NKDA.
Exam: lungs with mild expiratory prolongation; heart regular without murmur; healed sternotomy and right hip incisions; no edema.
Prevention: high-dose flu and updated COVID today. Colonoscopy due 2028. LDCT due January. Pneumococcal, shingles, Tdap, RSV done.
Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.
Next: chronic visit in early 2026.

documents.title: Wellness labs

documents.body: Everything normal on this year's labs, cholesterol unchanged. Good to see you walking so well.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Visit 2/12/2026. Received by fax 2/13/2026.

CC: lightheaded, wiped out.
HPI: 69M discharged from our medical floor 2/10 after 5 days for a COPD flare, treated with oral prednisone, tiotropium and nebulized bronchodilators. Metoprolol was increased in hospital for runs of tachycardia; went home with new prescriptions filled at his own pharmacy. Over the last two days he has felt dizzy on standing and exhausted. On review of his bottles at the bedside, he has been taking the new metoprolol succinate 50 mg tablet each morning and also his old 25 mg tablet - 'I thought the new one was extra.' No syncope, chest pain, or worsening breathing.
PMH: COPD group C, CAD with LAD stent and prior MIs, mitral repair with ring 10/2024, postoperative cardiogenic shock 6/2025, HTN, HLD. Right THA 6/2025.
Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate as above, tiotropium, albuterol PRN, prednisone (last dose due 2/11).
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals on arrival: BP 95/60, HR 48, RR 20.
Exam: alert, conversant. Bradycardic, regular. Lungs without wheeze or crackles. No edema. Neuro nonfocal. Otherwise unremarkable.
ECG: sinus bradycardia, no AV block, no acute changes.
Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.0, glucose 98, hemoglobin 14.

Impression: beta-blocker toxicity from unintended duplicate metoprolol dosing after discharge.
Course: metoprolol held. Monitored on telemetry; no intervention needed. HR 64 and orthostatic symptoms resolved by evening.
Disposition: home. Take metoprolol succinate 25 mg only, restarting tomorrow; discard the 50 mg tablets. See PCP this week.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED fax reviewed with PCP. Reached pt. Feels steadier this morning. Took ONE metoprolol 25 mg today as instructed. 50 mg bottle is in a bag to bring to his visit. Teach-back done: one metoprolol, the 25. He had not called back about our voicemail because he 'figured it was about the CT.' Lung CT for today cancelled, will rebook after recovery. PCP visit Tuesday 2/17.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

documents.title: Post-ED visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two hospital contacts in a week, neither of which we were told about at the time: 5-day COPD admission 2/5-2/10 (we learned from a pharmacy fill notice 2/11 - no discharge summary yet), then ED 2/12 for dizziness/fatigue with HR 48, BP 95/60. ED record received 2/13: he'd been taking the new 50 mg metoprolol succinate plus his old 25 mg.

Today: dizziness gone since Friday. Energy coming back. Breathing back to his usual; finished prednisone 2/11. Using albuterol once or twice a day this week, tapering off. No chest pain, no syncope.

Bag of bottles reviewed one by one: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 25, tiotropium, albuterol. The 50 mg metoprolol bottle (27 tablets left) taken out of his supply; he agreed to drop it in the pharmacy disposal bin. Updated printed med list given; pillbox refilled in the room with him.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Lungs: prolonged expiration, scattered end-expiratory wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. Beta-blocker toxicity from duplicate metoprolol - resolved. Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily only. Asked pharmacy to inactivate the 50 mg prescription.
2. COPD exacerbation requiring admission - recovered. Continue tiotropium, albuterol PRN. Discharge summary requested again.
3. CAD/HTN - stable.
Rebook the lung screening CT for spring. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Records follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Still no discharge summary for 2/5-2/10 admission. Called hospital HIM: told the summary 'is not showing as signed' yet. Third request faxed. ED record from 2/12 already on file.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: annual lung cancer screening, former smoker. Comparison: 1/10/2025.
Technique: low-dose helical CT without contrast.
Findings: No pulmonary nodule. Mild upper-lobe emphysema, unchanged. No consolidation or effusion. Sternal wires and mitral annuloplasty ring. LAD stent with coronary calcification. Heart size normal. No adenopathy.

documents.title: Lung CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lung screening CT is negative again. Nothing new since last year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months after the February admission and ED visit. No more dizziness. One metoprolol a day - showed me the pillbox. Breathing at baseline, albuterol a few times a week. Walking again, hip feels great. Cardiology moved his winter visit to September because of the admission. February discharge summary never came despite three requests; not chasing further.
No chest pain, orthopnea or edema.
Exam: lungs with prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P: COPD group C - stable on tiotropium + PRN albuterol. CAD/mitral repair - stable on aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 25. BP fine. CMP, CBC, lipids today. Wellness visit in September.
